\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Circuit Reindex}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.LMN.CircuitReindex
\section{Overview}

This module provides infrastructure for re-indexing the gate inputs of a Boolean
circuit: it defines an operation that maps the variable indices of a circuit through
a function $f : \mathrm{Fin}\,m \to \mathrm{Fin}\,m'$, and proves that this operation
preserves circuit depth and commutes with evaluation.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Re-indexing a circuit]
\lean{BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.reidx}
\label{BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.reidx}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit}
Given a circuit $c$ on $m$ variables and a function $f : \mathrm{Fin}\,m \to \mathrm{Fin}\,m'$,
the re-indexed circuit $\mathrm{reidx}(c, f)$ on $m'$ variables is obtained by replacing
each literal index $i$ by $f(i)$ (keeping its sign) and recursing structurally through the
$\mathrm{And}/\mathrm{Or}$ nodes.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Reindexing preserves circuit depth]
\lean{BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.reidx_depth}
\label{BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.reidx_depth}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit, BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.depth, BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.ind, BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.reidx}
\difficulty{5}
Let $m,m'$ be natural numbers, let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $m$ variables, and let
$f$ map the $m$ input indices to the $m'$ input indices. Replacing each input index of
$c$ by its image under $f$ preserves depth.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reindexing commutes with evaluation]
\lean{BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.reidx_eval}
\label{BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.reidx_eval}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.Lit.eval, BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit, BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.eval, BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.ind, BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.reidx}
\difficulty{5}
Let $m,m'$ be natural numbers, let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $m$ variables, let $f :
\mathrm{Fin}\,m \to \mathrm{Fin}\,m'$, and let $g : \mathrm{Fin}\,m' \to \bbf_2$ be an
assignment. Evaluating the reindexed circuit under $g$ gives the same value as
evaluating $c$ under the assignment $g \circ f$.
\end{theorem}
